title: Mandua ki Roti
steps: Mix mandua flour with salt and hot water to form a soft dough. Knead well.
Pat into thick rotis by hand and cook on a hot tawa till done on both sides.
Serve hot, smeared with ghee if desired, with dal or sabzi.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Nutritious gluten-free millet flatbread – a winter and everyday staple of the hills.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Hand-patted texture is traditional.

title: Aloo ke Gutke
steps: Cube the boiled potatoes. Heat mustard oil, add jakhiya seeds and let them crackle.
Add red chilli, turmeric and the potatoes. Toss on high heat till coated and slightly crisp.
Finish with coriander. Serve with puri, roti or as a snack.

fullIngredients.name: Jakhiya seeds, red chilli, coriander, turmeric, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic Kumaoni/Garhwali potato dish – the crackle of jakhiya is signature.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Mustard oil is essential for authentic flavour.

title: Gahat Stuffed Roti
steps: Prepare a spiced paste from cooked gahat (kulath/horse gram). Stuff into wheat dough, seal and roll into parathas.
Cook on a tawa with ghee till golden.
Serve hot with curd or chutney.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Protein-rich stuffed flatbread using the local horse gram.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Filling and warming for cold mornings.

title: Kafuli
steps: Wash and roughly chop the greens. Cook with a little water, garlic and chilli till soft.
Mash or blend lightly. Add rice paste to thicken and simmer.
Temper with cumin in ghee. Serve with rice or roti – a classic green curry of the hills.

fullIngredients.name: Rice paste or flour for thickening

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iron-rich, creamy green preparation – traditionally cooked in iron vessels.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: One of the most representative dishes of Uttarakhand.

title: Chainsoo
steps: Dry-roast the urad dal till aromatic, then grind coarsely. Cook with water, turmeric and salt till thick.
Temper generously with garlic, cumin and red chilli in ghee.
Serve with rice or mandua roti – a high-protein Garhwali classic.

fullIngredients.name: Garlic, cumin, red chilli, turmeric, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Roasting the dal before cooking is the key step for depth of flavour.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Hearty and warming.

title: Bhatt ki Churkani
steps: Cook the soaked black soybeans till soft. Mash lightly or leave whole.
Thicken with rice paste and simmer into a rich gravy. Add buttermilk for a slight tang if desired.
Temper with garlic and cumin in ghee. Serve with rice or roti.

fullIngredients.name: Rice paste or flour, buttermilk (optional), spices

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Signature Garhwali black-soybean curry – earthy, protein-rich and deeply satisfying.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A winter favourite.

title: Phaanu
steps: Soak mixed lentils overnight, grind coarsely and cook slowly with water and salt till thick and soft.
Temper with garlic, cumin and chilli in ghee.
Serve with rice – a wholesome, slow-cooked lentil dish of Garhwal.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Healthy mixed-lentil preparation – often considered one of the most nutritious local dishes.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Long, slow cooking develops the best texture.

title: Gahat ki Dal
steps: Pressure-cook the soaked gahat till soft. Mash lightly if desired.
Temper with garlic and cumin in ghee. Simmer briefly.
Serve with rice or mandua roti – a robust, warming dal.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Horse gram is a local staple valued for its nutrition and warming properties.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Simple tempering lets the dal shine.

title: Arsa
steps: Soak rice, grind into a paste. Cook jaggery into a thick syrup and mix with the rice paste to form a dough.
Shape into small discs and deep-fry till golden and crisp.
Cool and store. A festive sweet of both Kumaon and Garhwal.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional rice-jaggery sweet – crisp outside with a chewy, sweet interior.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Made for festivals and special occasions.

title: Bal Mithai
steps: Cook khoya with sugar till it thickens and darkens into a fudge-like consistency.
Shape into small cubes or rectangles and coat with white roasted sugar balls.
The iconic chocolate-like sweet of Kumaon (though it contains no chocolate).

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Famous Almora speciality – dark, fudgy and coated with tiny sugar balls.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best bought from traditional sweet shops for authentic texture.

title: Bhang ki Chutney
steps: Dry-roast the hemp seeds. Grind with green chilli, garlic, salt and a souring agent into a coarse or smooth chutney.
Adjust consistency with a little water. Serve as a pungent, flavourful accompaniment.

fullIngredients.name: Green chilli, garlic, lemon or amchur, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Distinctive Pahadi chutney – earthy, slightly bitter and very local.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Pairs especially well with aloo ke gutke and mandua roti.

title: Thechwani
steps: Crush or roughly pound the radish (and potato if using). Heat mustard oil, add jakhiya and spices.
Add the crushed vegetables and cook till soft and well-flavoured.
Serve with roti or rice – a rustic Garhwali preparation.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The name comes from ‘thechna’ (to crush) – the texture is deliberately coarse.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Simple, peppery and very local.
